title: Reported price adaptations persist and re-enter at different rates across financial-condition paths
source_unit: Recontacted SHED respondent with shared shedid and nonmissing 2025 panel weight; weighted descriptive paired record

observations.period: 2024 to 2025; financial condition worsened; persistence among 2024 prior adopters

cheaper_products.unit: weighted percent among 512 valid prior-adopter pairs

used_less_or_stopped.unit: weighted percent among 488 valid prior-adopter pairs

reduced_savings.unit: weighted percent among 327 valid prior-adopter pairs

increased_borrowing.unit: weighted percent among 140 valid prior-adopter pairs

delayed_major_purchase.unit: weighted percent among 378 valid prior-adopter pairs

observations.method: Official Federal Reserve SHED 2024 and 2025 CSV releases; shared shedid paired by scripts/analyze_shed_panel_adaptation_condition_path.py; financial-condition movement classified as worsened, same broad condition, or improved; weighted 2025 Yes share among 2024 Yes respondents.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted persistence estimate with no replicate-weight standard errors or causal identification; metric-specific valid-pair denominators apply.
observations.subgroup: Respondents whose ordered financial-condition category moved downward, among those reporting each adaptation in 2024.
observations.counterinterpretation: Worsening may select people with prior severe pressure, health, care, employment, debt, or housing changes; persistence is not caused by the condition transition.

observations.period: 2024 to 2025; financial condition stayed in the same broad category; persistence among 2024 prior adopters

cheaper_products.unit: weighted percent among 1646 valid prior-adopter pairs

reduced_savings.unit: weighted percent among 1050 valid prior-adopter pairs

increased_borrowing.unit: weighted percent among 318 valid prior-adopter pairs

observations.method: Same paired SHED procedure and weighted outcome definition as the adjacent condition-path observations.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted persistence estimate with no replicate-weight standard errors or causal identification; metric-specific valid-pair denominators apply.
observations.subgroup: Respondents whose ordered financial-condition category stayed in the same broad category, among those reporting each adaptation in 2024.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable category does not mean stable income, prices, health, care, debt, or material conditions within the category.

observations.period: 2024 to 2025; financial condition improved; persistence among 2024 prior adopters

cheaper_products.unit: weighted percent among 553 valid prior-adopter pairs

used_less_or_stopped.unit: weighted percent among 544 valid prior-adopter pairs

reduced_savings.unit: weighted percent among 400 valid prior-adopter pairs

increased_borrowing.unit: weighted percent among 173 valid prior-adopter pairs

delayed_major_purchase.unit: weighted percent among 447 valid prior-adopter pairs

observations.method: Same paired SHED procedure and weighted outcome definition as the adjacent condition-path observations.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted persistence estimate with no replicate-weight standard errors or causal identification; metric-specific valid-pair denominators apply.
observations.subgroup: Respondents whose ordered financial-condition category moved upward, among those reporting each adaptation in 2024.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improvement is not recovery from every adaptation; debt, care, health, housing, or durable changes in need may sustain behavior.

boundary: This record preserves a 4,419-person descriptive SHED panel comparison. It covers persistence among prior adopters; the companion memo also reports re-entry among prior non-adopters. It does not establish causality, household-level outcomes, or a single stress score across distinct adaptations.
